item.title: SCP idea, seeking greenlight: The Grand Conspiracy: SCP idea, seeking greenlight: The Grand Conspiracy
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An infohazard that causes no side effects whatsoever unless someone tries to look into the nature of its existence. Anyone who attempts such will become more and more unstable as they begin to obsess over researching the SCP, coming up with theories concerning it that become increasingly irrational as their mental state decreases, eventually driving them to insanity. Essentially, the SCP makes anyone who tries to figure out what it is into a deranged conspiracy theorist.

Central Narrative: The perspective of an unfortunate researcher, showcasing his descent into insanity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP isn’t one of those "kills you as soon as you realize it exists" things - it works by lowering your intellect/mental stability until you're not able to even come close to understanding it. For example, an experienced scientist might start off with a somewhat accurate hypothesis, only to wind up believing that it was created by Hitler's secret grandchild in Area 51 a week later. And considering that it has no outward anomalous effects, it could potentially have already infected every person on the planet undetected - alternatively, it could be some kind of virus with a malicious purpose that the Foundation will never be able to come close to discovering.

Additional Notes: I haven't yet figured out some parts of this, like how exactly the Foundation would discover this SCP exists - I can work out the finer details when I start drafting. For now, I just want to know if this would be something people are interested in reading.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: SCP idea: Seeking Greenlight: SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): vehicle / extradimensional / ad-astra

Elevator Pitch: A dead space ship from the future, which has an invisible entity on board that kills everyone once it is in atmospheric environment.

Central Narrative: The SCP is divided into 2 parts, the ship and the entity. The ship is an advanced human design (not Foundation) that at the current time should not exist. The crew has been murdered by the entity and the ship has been vented. One of the Foundation researchers notes a couple of things about the ship (none of which are anomalous, making it unknow how it got to our time).

The entity can be heard walking around the ship and is pretty harmless in void. It can jump between ships and when in any atmosphere, arms come from the walls, pulling people inside the walls and killing them in the process. The entity was not originally on the ship, its origin is unknown.

The team sent to explore the ship finds disfigured humans basically melted into the ships structure. After a while the team is killed by the entity except for 2 members who still die after a while because they run out of oxygen and there is no help coming.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The entity on board the ship is only dangerous under atmospheric pressure but humans need that to survive.

Additional Notes: Hope it's not too generic horror.

item.title: A Face full of Stars: A Face full of Stars
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama, Mystery.

Elevator Pitch: Robotic entity, like a living humanoid machine, found in the middle of the forest in Sweden. The entity is in a dormant state until 2 members of the cult "The children of the Scarlet King" perform a ritual to awaken it.

Central Narrative: The SCP seems to be confused when it arrives at the Foundation. It doesn't know (or remember) what a human is. It has the ability to bend reality but does it rarely. The entity is somewhat dangerous but poses no real threat to the Foundation. However its memories slowly start to come back in small chunks… piecing together what it really is and why it is here.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It tries to assassinate SCP-999. What was the name of that cult again? The children of the Scarlet King? Perhaps there's something bigger here… something that will be added in containment breach logs and interviews later in the future.

Additional Notes: Assassinate is a strong word. It more just attacks SCP-999 having no idea why it does this. Of course the attempt fails and the entity just gets itself hurt.

The scp is also known as "A Face full of Stars because the SCP greatly resembles that of a robotic entity from a reboot of a old tv show about traveling space. The netflix lost in space reboot.

One of the addendums, explaining how the scp was discovered, also slightly explains how the netflix reboot is actually made by one of the cultists who was given amnestic treatment and a fake name, but couldnt forget what the scp looked like.

item.title: Looking for Greenlight | The girl and her mysterious guardian: Looking for Greenlight | The girl and her mysterious guardian
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch: An invisible entity is connected to a human female.

Hook/ Attention-Grabber: The entity needs a human sacrifice every 42 days. If the 42 days deadline passes, the human female becomes ill (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, etc) until a few days later, where the entity will go on a killing spree of any humans in its general area.

Central Narrative: The entity first appeared to the human female when she was in a park. After this encounter, the human became infatuated with the entity, resulting in it staying by her side at all times. 42 days after she met the creature, she became sick and soon dozens of people were dying, which caught the eye of the foundation.
After the foundation had made contact with the SCP, the female was taken into custody and her family and friends were told she died in a car crash.

Additional notes: I want the focus of the article to be the mystery of the entity and what it’s goals are.

item.title: I made my first scp!: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Hey Dreswrites: this is not the place for this. If you want to announce a SCP, you should use the announcements thread: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13597458/scp-announcements-46:aristotle-axolotl-throttle; or mention it in #site19 on IRC.

If you're looking for feedback on the SCP, I would direct you towards either #thecritters on IRC, or to the required reading for this forum: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas if you're wanting feedback on the idea as a whole. If you want feedback on the concept, you can edit this post (using the 'Edit' button under the blue 'Options' in the bottom right corner of the post, not the red 'Edit' at the bottom of the page) to use the required format.

Alternatively, the Swamp Critter Roster lists people who will give feedback on posted works.

item.title: Looking for Greenlights | The Stardust Solution: Looking for Greenlights | The Stardust Solution
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP, nicknamed "The Stardust Solution", is a microscopic singularity that is the first stage of a universe. It absorbs energy and matter at a subatomic level, increasing its density. At some point in time it will fail to contain its own density and explode instead of collapsing, creating a second Big Bang.

A stone tablet found near it indicates that some form of SCP created the singularity with the purpose of restarting the universe—for the second time.

Central Narrative: The article focuses on the perspective of two researchers assigned to this SCP—Doctors Stonewood and Jordan. The volatile nature of the SCP warrants the creation of a small Foundation outpost, as storing other SCPs near the singularity is hazardous.

After describing the discovery of the SCP, the file turns to a series of interviews.

Interview One presents Stonewood and Jordan as colleagues speaking about the threat the singularity presents. As Jordan explains the nature of the SCP to Stonewood, he articulates that he has given up hope. The singularity will continue absorbing energy until it ruptures, and they know nothing about how to stop it. Jordan also believes that it doesn't deserve to be an SCP—the phenomena is a natural state of the universe (they have not yet translated the stone tablet).

Stonewood is far more optimistic, and he convinces Jordan to help him develop a way to slow down the singularity, limiting the likelihood that it will rupture anytime soon. The interview ends on a hopeful note—despite not knowing how to stop the anomaly from eventually rupturing and causing an XK scenario, they pledge themselves to seeking the answers.

Interview Two is set six months later. The stone tablet has been restored and is now readable, and Stonewood is interviewing the linguist who translated it. The linguist gives Stonewood the translation written in English. Upon reading it, he grows agitated and leaves the interview, seeking Doctor Jordan.

The addendum reveals the translation: a command from a being ordering his "son" to erase the "narrative" that he sees as a failure. The writing ends with a vow: "I promise I will not make the same mistakes the third time around."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation has dealt with a ridiculous amount of anomalies, but it made me wonder: what if another SCP got sick of living in a world full of anomalies and decided to try to "correct" it?

item.title: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper: Re: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper
item.content:encoded:
Hey, there. Let's take a look, shall we?

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

This feels like an alternate take of the story of the Thumbling with an SCP subplot slapped on to remind the reader that this takes place in the Foundationverse. There's nothing wrong with taking inspiration from old fairy tales, but, coming from someone who read Thumbling, I think this hits way too close to home for its own good.

Also, befriending a girl who would later grow up to be O5 is…kinda convenient. Kinda extremely convenient. Possible? I suppose. Plausible? Probably not.

Even if we got over the convenience of this Thumbling befriending a future O5, I fully believe they'd still contain him. The Foundation exists to contain. Even if the O5 girl was friends with him pre-containment, as cold as it sounds, she'd most definitely put this dangerous and highly prestigious job over her old friend. She'd have to if she wanted to keep her job.

Even if she did break protocol, there are 12 other O5 Council members who would most definitely outvote her.

I absolutely do not buy them letting this random thumb-sized man help out around the Foundation. They have personnel.

Honestly…I don't know what advice to offer. This is too close to an actual existing fairytale, I feel like. I'm not sure how to improve this and I'm always hesitant to tell someone to scrap an idea.

I suggest reaching out to someone on the butterfly squad roster and trying to get a second opinion.

Anywho, I apologise if this was harsh, but I do hope I helped! 👍

Have a good one!

item.title: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA - Greenlights needed!: Re: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA - Greenlights needed!
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM

The premise of sirens as weird ads is alright - it's an interesting enough play on the ideas when mixed together, I guess. Unfortunately, the intrigue this builds up is immediately undercut by just having them be monsters that will kill you. Whilst expected given the premise is essentially sirens, it's still just far too standard - murder monsters just aren't very interesting any more, and the vast majority of the site audience will need a lot of convincing to enjoy that kind of article.

The idea of sirens adapting to the modern world is fun, and it's a decent premise for a narrative I think, but you don't do enough with it to really make it work. There's no actual story here, no real series of events, only a premise that might start a narrative. You need to fill out the rest of what's going to happen - tell us the middle and the end of the story too. What's the progression and the arc here? That's the key information we need to know to be confident in the story.

I think you need to put a bit of thought into how you're going to get the reader involved in the story here - whilst the premise is intriguing, it's lacking something to really latch onto because it carries neither mystery nor character really. I'd recommend trying to involve more character into the story so that you can really get the reader involved and caring about your story. The premise might do that, but without something more substantive, I wouldn't be confident it could carry a reader the whole way through the story.

Good luck!

item.title: Men Are Expendable: Re: Men Are Expendable
item.content:encoded:
Hi ! Thanks for the crit ! :)

+ show block
– hide block

So the biggest problem with the concept behind your anomaly is that it isn't actually anomalous. Human Parthenogenesis (also known as human asexual reproduction) has been proven to be a viable reproductive option for humans. This is obviously a somewhat large problem (the concept behind your anomaly isn't actually anomalous), but for now I'll crit what else is there.

Well, from my understanding all the attempts for Human Parthenogenesis have always resulted in a production of unvialable embryos (in which case the effects of my object is indeed anomalous).
In case I'm wrong, I will try to find another interesting idea.

+ show block
– hide block

This is a bit vague, but from what I'm getting this ritual will terminate another woman's pregnancy to activate the target's own pregnancy. Are there any ways of choosing which woman has their pregnancy stolen, or is it random?

It is random. To be absolutely honest, my initial draft for this idea is a bit longer, but I had to rewrite in order to not exceed the limit of 400 words.

+ show block
– hide block

Also, this brings up a logistical problem: you say that the whole concept behind this anomaly is women reproducing without men, but how is this possible in a remote African village where methods of parthenogenesis aren't available? Basically, if the ritual requires the 'stealing' of another pregnancy, and there is no way to have asexual pregnancies in the setting, then wouldn't men be needed for this ritual for initial fertilisation, thus rendering the primary theme of this concept1 null and void? ALSO also, what does 'special' mean in this context?

I mean, the whole concept of this object is that it allows a women to become pregnant. Why would they need to know about the scientific concept of Parthenogenesis ? The specific knowledge of this concept is not a requirement for the object to work. So I don't really understand your remarque here.
As for the stealing, I admit that this part is poorly developed. I will try to make it better.

Finally, the 'special' part is specified in the first line of my narrative. Basically, the children resulting from the pregnancy are what we would call "humans in great shape", but also presenting great logical thinking.

Also : I really want to develop this idea further, but I can't go beyond the 400 words limit. So I will try to be more concise in my next idea draft.
